data.narrative:
Picogrid, a Series A-stage frontier-technology company in Defense & Security, is evaluated against a peer universe of ten same-sector companies spanning Series B and adjacent stages. The comparative set includes eight private companies and two public equities (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS), with notable peers including Anduril Industries, Shield AI, and Helsing.

Two valuation methods are applied. Stage-progression methodology, using the $45M+ total raised as a proxy base value, applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for Series A advancement, yielding $90M. Peer-median analysis across the ten-company sample produces a $1.0B implied valuation, with peer range spanning $125M to $3.0B. The peer distribution reflects substantial heterogeneity within the Defense & Security tech sector at comparable stages.

Triangulation of these methods supports a valuation range of $76M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median point of $545M. The wide dispersion—reflecting both the early-stage uncertainty inherent in Series A and the variance in peer outcomes—indicates material sensitivity to deal-specific factors including technology differentiation, customer traction, and capital efficiency relative to comparable cohort. Key uncertainties center on revenue trajectory visibility and competitive positioning within a consolidating defense-tech landscape.
